Color-Coded for Your Convenience: It's no wonder he's dressed entirely in black. Freudian Excuse: He was an unwanted child, so he grew up as an orphan with no name and no one to care for him. This isTruth in Televisiondue to China's one-child policy.

characters.name: No. 85: The Courier
characters.description: The perfect middleman, he's aOne-Man Armyfor hire. He's used by the bad guys and government alike operating in a black ops capacity to ensure that an operation is successful.Just don't get in his way or he'll go out of his way to hunt you down and make you pay. Abusive Parents: His father would strike him and his brother, but since Tommy felt no pain, his father didn't feel like he had sufficient control over him. So he entered himinto dogfights. Ax-Crazy: His own brother thinks he snapped long ago. Character Death: Gets killed due to several gunshot wounds and the loss of blood. Crazy-Prepared: He takes advantage of hisFeel No Painpower to carry an escape kitinside his own skin.

characters.name: No. 86: Sir Crispin Crandall
characters.description: Artistic License – Biology: An in-universe example thereof as he's betting heavily on cryogenics working before it's proven to be so. Insane Troll Logic: Forgets that cryogenic freezing isn't actually a form of suspended animation but a method ofpreserving corpses. As such, gets a monumental"The Reason You Suck" Speechfrom Red who points out he's just been murdering geniuses needed to advance humanity. "The Reason You Suck" Speech: Gets a great one from Red who points out the idiocy of how, when the day humanity's fall occurs, the people who could have stopped it will have been trapped in freezing and that "betting on the future is a sucker's game". Well-Intentioned Extremist: How he sees himself but Red says he's just a nutcase.

characters.name: No. 87: Quon Zhang
characters.description: Bald of Evil: Sports this, being played by Ron Yuan, who himself is bald. Dark and Troubled Past: He has endured in horrible conditions back in China working in factories. Red Herring: The FBI (and Reddington) thinks that he's stealing dead bodies of Chinese-American women just to smuggle things. While it was true, Zhang insisted that it was only a diversion to smuggle a Russian agent into American soil.

characters.name: No. 88: Ivan
characters.description: The Cracker: A world-class computer hacker who can afford (and therefore has likely stolen or illegally obtained) $8 million payouts, can rob accounts in the Cayman Islands, has crashed Russian markets, sold government secrets, and disrupted Siberian pipelines. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Red makes a passing mention to Ivan having a brother, with the implication that they are sometime partners-in-crime. Karma Houdini: Last seen on a plane with Reddington. It's likely Red was planning to hand him over to the Feds once he'd given them the Skeleton Key, but since he had nothing to do with that it's entirely likely that Red let him go. Husky Russkie: Though given his hatred of Russia it's not clear if he is actually Russian (and has a problem with the current government), a separatist of some sort, or from one of Russia's neighbours (his actor is ethnic Russian-Ukrainian and Reddington meets him in Belarus). Noodle Incident: The aforementioned theft of $5 million from Reddington. That Ivan doesn't appear to recognise Reddington at first crosses this over withBut for Me, It Was Tuesday.

characters.name: No. 89: Dr. James Covington
characters.description: Once one of America's preeminent cardiothoracic surgeons, Dr. James Covington was all about saving lives until he tried to transplant adult lungs into a dying little girl and lost his license. Then he went off the grid, setting up an illegal transplant ring, one-stop shopping for anyone in need of a lifesaving organ unavailable through traditional channels. The catch? Covington "leased" his organs for an exorbitant fee, which he donated to children's charities. If clients couldn't pay, their organs were "repossessed," causing their deaths. Anti-Villain: His organ loan shark ring ishorrificbut he raises a lot of valid points and uses the money to fund his work for the disadvantaged. Evil Debt Collector: He doesn'tsellhis illegally acquired donor organs, herentsthem. If a former client can't pay the 500K/year fees, he tracks them down and takes the organs back. Fallen Hero: Lost his license to practice medicine when he diverted a donor organ so that he could implant it in a critically ill child. The child lived, the intended donor didn't. Graceful Loser: Dr. Covington allowed himself to be arrested after he was able to perform an operation on a child in his underground hospital.

characters.name: No. 90: The Travel Agency
characters.description: The Hunter Becomes the Hunted:The killer seen in the episode is an amnesiac member of the defunct agency who is being manipulated into killing its operatives by his wife. Professional Killer: Their business.

characters.name: No. 91: The Ethicist
characters.description: Awesomeness by Analysis: Say what you will about his cold-blooded mindset, he proves genuinely observant when he realizes that Liz finding him is part of a rogue investigation. Cold Equation: His whole thing is killing people in order to, in his view, benefit society more than if the victim had lived. Deadly Doctor: He first came to the attention of the law when he worked as a doctor and euthanized several patients. The authoritiesfigured he was an Angel of Death who killed them because he thought he was ending their pain, but it was actually because they had signed up for more treatment and he believed the resources needed to treat them would be better spent on other patients. Dissonant Serenity: Tells a woman about home accident rates among women - while killing her and staging it as a slip in the shower. Face Death with Dignity: Convinces Liz to let him kill himself rather than go to prison, and is completely unmoved by it.

characters.name: No. 92: The Brockton College Killer
characters.description: Dead Guy on Display: Left her victims on display in public areas after they were completely frozen. Freudian Excuse: Her method of killing comes from an incident from her childhood when the "popular girls" at a birthday party locked her in a freezer for an hour. Locked in a Freezer: Kills her victims by knocking them out, locking them in a freezer and freezing them to death by saturating them in liquid nitrogen. Samus Is a Girl: Is a woman, though the killer was presumed to be male (as serial killers most often are). Yandere: Killed her victims because she thought they were attracted to Tobias Carlyle, with whom she was obsessed.

characters.name: No. 93: The Deer Hunter
characters.description: Actually two separate individuals. The original Deer Hunter was a serial killer, who stalked strong men that reminded him of his abusive father. He murdered his victims with a bow-and-arrow before gutting them, stringing them up, and taking a single bite out of their liver. The second is a copycat, and the original's wife, who killed him and uses the identity to strike at obsessive and abusive husbands and boyfriends. Anti-Villain: It's hard not to sympathize with the second Deer Hunter. Automatic Crossbows: The killer's main weapon of choice. Crazy Cat Lady: The copycat has multiple cats (and even a bird) she voices her rationalizations to. Informed Flaw: Both are profiled as physically weakLong Range Fighters. But for a "physically weak" person, the copycat sure can swing blunt objects hard enough to KO people, then even drag one —Liz— all the way back home.And while Liz does end up beating her, it's visibly due to skill instead of strength.

characters.name: No. 94: T. Earl King VI
characters.description: The patriarch of a centuries-old criminal dynasty, who amasses their wealth by holding criminal auctions of stolen merchandise ranging from priceless Van Gogh artwork to yellowcake uranium to living beings. Been There, Shaped History: Reddington claims that the King family was involved in the disappearance ofRaoul Wallenberg. Big, Screwed-Up Family: A group of evil auctioneers who systematically force its members to risk suicide. Character Death: Earl is shot by Reddington with the revolver that his family had used to settle the score after the auction; might qualify as aKarmic Death. Eccentric Millionaire: The King family's public image is that they're just a group of eccentric trust fund millionaires.

characters.name: No. 95: Mr. Gregory Devry
characters.description: Con Man:According to Red, he was a talented grifter. Good All Along:In reality, he's Red's friend. Passing himself for Reddington was actually a plan devised by both him and Red, in order to help Raymond to keep hiding his relationship with the FBI and to keep a good reputation among other criminals. As an added bonus, thanks to him, Raymond was also able to make another crime boss (the one who was the most suspicious) his scapegoat and to kill him. Heroic Sacrifice:He allows himself to be killed so that Red can keep hiding his relationship with the FBI. The Last Dance:He has terminal cancer. He chose to die while taking part to his best con. Secretly Dying:Only Red knew he had terminal cancer. That's the reason why they devised this plan.

characters.name: No. 97: The Longevity Initiative
characters.description: Driven to Suicide: Dr. Julian Powell shoots himself rather risking being incarcerated. The Needs of the Many: How Dr. Powell justifies the kidnappings and experimenting on random bystanders.

characters.name: No. 98:Dr Adrian Shaw
characters.description: Samus Is a Girl: Despite her male alias, she is a woman named Sonia Bloom.

characters.name: No. 99: Minister D
characters.description: Character Name Alias: His alias comes from the villain of theEdgar Allan Poestory "The Purloined Letter". Good Scars, Evil Scars: Is a criminal and has a big scar on his left cheek. Only Known by Their Nickname: He is only known by his pseudonym until he is captured. Sinister Surveillance: He gains blackmail leverage on his marks by bugging their phones.

characters.name: No. 100: Abraham Stern
characters.description: A thief who has spent the better part of his life searching for a treasure his father hid and left clues for. Blackmail: Uses his position as a loan officer to force loantakers to aid in his search for the treasure by threatening them with foreclosure and offering to extend their loans. Chronic Backstabbing Disorder: Betrays just about everyone who works with him, including Reddington, who is probably only allowed to live because Stern liked him. Gentleman Thief: Dresses nicely, is polite and works at a bank, but is ruthless enough to kill to further his plan. My Greatest Failure: His father bequeathed him the four pennies that made out the map to the treasure - and, being a dumb teenager at the time, he spent them on candy only to find out about the map a month later.

characters.name: No. 101: The Alchemist
characters.description: A disgraced scientist who now puts his skills to use by helping bad people disappear. Character Death: Gets killed by his own wife with a revolver taken from an armed civilian. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Ultimately averted. He has more concern for himself than his family, whom he is possessive of. Faux Affably Evil: He can come across as semi-charming, but there's a definite level of slime beneath the veneer. Jerkass: Trettel is a smug bastard who cares more about getting his immunity than saving his daughter's life.

characters.name: No. 102: The Harem
characters.description: Fallen Hero: Margot is acorrections officer turned rogue. Incompatible Orientation: Margot attempting to seduceLizin the bathroom and being turned down. Karmic Thief: The Harem only steal from other criminals and thieves, but only to cover their tracks. Lipstick Lesbian: Margot as she states that she has had girlfriends and when she attempts to make a pass atLizin the bathroom. The Mole: Liz when she infiltrates the group and it is also revealed thatEmmais a former British agent who is also secretly working for Red to spy on the group.

characters.name: No. 103: Alistair Pitt
characters.description: Ambiguously Gay: He hasCamp Gaymannerisms with the way he dresses, walks, and talks, but his sexuality is never clarified. Arranged Marriage: He invokes this to get rival crime families to become one family and merge their businesses. Character Death: Shot and killed by Reddington. It's Personal: Red has him on the Blacklist and goes after him because he arranged for Josephine Molire/Moliere, an old love of Red's and the daughter of an Eastern European arms dealer to be married to Gabriel Stockwell, who was abusive and he beat her to the point that she is now fully paralyzed and catatonic in a wheel chair. Pet the Dog: Literally as he always has his two pet dogs with him everywhere he goes and is even shown bathing with them.

characters.name: No. 104: Lord Baltimore
characters.description: A tracker by trade, Lord Baltimore's methods were cutting edge. Formerly thought by the world to be male, she made an art of combing cyberspace — finding status updates, financial records and location blips — all the digital traces that virtually everyone leaves behind. Using data analytics algorithms, she built dossiers on people who didn't want to be found... and then dealt with them, per her clients' request. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Due to herSplit Personality. Character Name Alias: Her nickname seems to come fromButch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid, in which it is the name of a largely unseen Native American tracker who is said to be able to track down anyone and is part of the posse pursuing the title characters. Cold Sniper: Lord Baltimore is handy with a rifle. Domestic Abuse: Nora was raped by an uncle as a child.

characters.name: No. 105: The Lindquist Concern
characters.description: The Dog Was the Mastermind:Turns out the one responsible for being in the blacklist was just a mild-mannered employee of a patent office.

characters.name: No. 106: The Good Samaritan
characters.description: Abusive Parents: He suffered under the wrath of an abusive mother. All Crimes Are Equal: FromDomestic Abusersto a mom whose kid was injured playing hockey. It's all the same to him. Anti-Villain: Is aVigilante Manseeking to make abusers pay viaA Taste of Their Own Medicine. He's still quite a creepy bastard about it, though. Apologetic Attacker: Not directly to his victim, but it still counts. Character Death: The FBI kills him after he gets cornered.

characters.name: No. 107: The Architect
characters.description: Cool Old Guy: Fairly old, and comfortable around hackers much younger than him. Fiery Cover-Up: He seems to have a habit of committing great acts of destruction to cover up comparatively small crimes; Reddington credits him with blowing up a tanker full of diesel fuel and flooding a district in London just to steal diamonds, and causing a fatal avalanche to cover up the theft of a painting. No Name Given: We never learn his real name.

characters.name: No. 108: Kings of the Highway
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: Jilly; even Red tells her she needs help. Chronic Backstabbing Disorder: They tend to turn on each other; the higher the payoff, the sooner the betrayal.Although it's somewhat zigzagged. The reason why one of them betrays and killshis leaderwas partly because he didn't want toabandon an other member of the gang who had been captured by Liz, who used him as a bargaining chip to free Reddington. Although it's somewhat zigzagged. The reason why one of them betrays and killshis leaderwas partly because he didn't want toabandon an other member of the gang who had been captured by Liz, who used him as a bargaining chip to free Reddington. Jerkass: They're all pretty nasty in their own ways. Not-So-Harmless Villain: Even if it was because of blind luck, they still managed to captureReddington himself. That's a feat a lot of more intelligent, powerful and influential people couldn't do.

characters.name: No. 109: General Ludd
characters.description: Anti-Villain: While they are responsible for innocent people's deaths, their motives are presented sympathetically. Bomb-Throwing Anarchists: A modern example. Their overall goal is anarchy, if only to bring down the capitalist oligarchies than political ethos. Crazy-Prepared: How the group survived despite efforts by police and the FBI to apprehend their members. The Chessmaster: Their (incredibly elaborate) planvery nearlysucceeds, with them outwitting the FBI twice, only losing due to Reddington's intervention. Fictional Counterpart: To Anonymous; the masks are different as they are actually the IP of Warner Bros. This may be zigzagged though; the General Ludd group is fairly small and could easily be hiding in plain sight among other activists.

characters.name: No. 110: Nicholas T. Moore
characters.description: ACultleader who leads a hidden, isolated village whose citizens believe the outside world has been destroyed by a great disaster. Church of Happyology: Beingan unsuccessful sci-fi writer, and having his followers isolated from the rest of the world, there are some parallels between Moore andL. Ron Hubbard, the founder of Scientology. Con Artist: He is fully aware that the story he enforces on his village is a complete crock. Driven to Suicide:Commits suicide in custody with a smuggled suicide pill. From Nobody to Nightmare: Went from beinga failed sci-fi authorto running a brainwashed cult and tricking them into thinking the outside world is a post-apocalyptic wasteland.

characters.name: No. 112: Monarch Douglas Bank
characters.description: The preferred bank ofinternational criminals, dictators, terrorists and hedge fund managersis headquartered in the United States, with branches in 63 countries and deposits insured by the FDIC. The criminal division is run out of the unassuming Warsaw branch, legendary for laundering funds of the criminal elite without any traceable accounting and in full compliance. Corrupt Corporate Executive: Most of the bank's high-level executives are in on the take and/or are aware that the banks are being used by criminals and terrorists to launder and hide their money from law enforcement. Crazy-Prepared: In relation to keeping the Formula a secret from law enforcement. Government Conspiracy: The Bank launders dirty money both for corrupt governments and for shady black-ops programs... includingthe FBI Task Force. Karma Houdini: The Bank is never brought to justice and even though it loses its Formula, it is still permitted to go about its business by the end of the episode. That said, a lot of their customers might be very unhappy with them about losing access to their dirty money with the Formula gone.

characters.name: No. 113: Drexel
characters.description: Mad Artist: These days, his idea of art involves killing people and posing their bodies in dramatic ways.

characters.name: No. 114: The Mombasa Cartel
characters.description: An international cartel that does poaching on animals and sell exotic products on the market. Big, Screwed-Up Family: The enforcers for the cartel turn out to be a crazy family of animal rights extremists, a mother and her two sons, one of whom is a mentally handicappedPsychopathic Manchildwith a penchant forHunting the Most Dangerous Game. His father is her ex-lover, the head of the Cartel, and a public opponent of animal poaching. It's Personal: Red loathes the Cartel both for its cruelty to animals and for the fact that it ruthlessly massacres entire families and villages to enforce its will and more specifically, because one of those families belong to Dembe. The Hunter Becomes the Hunted: The cartel, which as made billions from poaching endangered animals and selling them on the black market, is having its members targeted for elimination by a radical animal rights group.Subvertedwhen it turns out its actually an internal purge of its members by its leader. Multinational Team: The cartel is made up of different nationalities.

characters.name: No. 115: Olivia Olson
characters.description: Evil Versus Evil: Her clientele is said to be criminals who hire her to take down other criminals (though the climax has her assist a company in discrediting an innocent civilian executive by framing her to look neglectful in the construction of a building). Karma Houdini: Escapes at the end of the episode.

characters.name: No. 116: General Shiro
characters.description: Beetle Maniac: Obsessed with insects and has genetically modified a species of beetle to be used as a deadly poison. Eaten Alive: The beetles he uses to kill people are administered as a poison in powder form, growing inside of the target and feeding of their insides until the victim dies and they exit through the mouth. Names to Run Away from Really Fast: His nickname comes fromSurgeon General Shirō Ishii, a Japanese medical officer duringWorld War IIwho was the director of Unit 731, a biological warfare division that, among other things, used plague-infested fleas as weapons. Well-Intentioned Extremist: His goal in his killings was to end the use of a dangerously effective pesticide because he saw the existence of insects as necessary to the functioning of nature and worth more than humans.

characters.name: No. 117: Vanessa Cruz
characters.description: The wife of an investor who got killed under strange circumstances, she personally wages a one-man war against the very investors responsible for his death. Anti-Villain: Is a bad guy, but is only after a certain number of investors and avenging her husband. Becoming the Mask: Vanessa ends up genuinely falling in love with a woman she intended to use as a pawn. Because of this, she's ultimately unable to go through with her vengeance scheme. Femme Fatale: She uses her sexuality as a powerful weapon to lure her targets in. Frame-Up: Vanessa specializes in framing people, and she'sverygood at it.

characters.name: Nos. 119-122: The Pavlovich Brothers
characters.description: Character Death: They get killed by Ressler and an FBISWATteam. Chekhov's Gunman: They were the men who were seen attack the FBI protection detail to kidnap Beth Ryker in the pilot. Red would later enlist them to kidnap Tom Keen. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: They do seem to care about each other. No Name Given: We never do find out their individual names. Punch-Clock Villain: They're just hirelings at the end of the day, and don't seem especially sadistic or cruel, just competent and amoral. Red is even able to hire them to capture Tom.

characters.name: No. 124: The Pharmacist
characters.description: Alliterative Name:SpaldingStark. Decoy Antagonist: As it turns out, he hasn't turned to fraud, as Reddington feared, and he isn't responsible for the deaths in the episode; they were the result of sabotage by his partner, Ethan Webb. Good All Along: While he experimented on humans, he genuinely wanted to create a working cure and only tested it on willing volunteers with few other good options. Professor Guinea Pig: He first became famous when he injected himself with a malaria vaccine he had developed, intending to let a malaria-infected mosquito sting him afterwards to prove that it worked. Unfortunately, this led to his current physical condition and need for a cane.

characters.name: No. 125: Hannah Hayes
characters.description: Alliterative Name:HannahHayes. Karmic Rape:Not literally rape, but the same level of violation and (in her case) end result. The men she and her accomplices kidnapped and impregnated were powerful, religious, socially conservative advocates (a priest, a politician and a lobbyist) who pushed for very restrictive abortion laws. After being impregnated, they were then kept imprisoned until the fetuses developed a heartbeat, at which point state laws would prohibit them from getting an abortion and even make them subject to prosecution if they had one out of state, which the politician does in the end. Mama Bear: Loves her daughter dearly,despite her origins. When Hannah is about to be arrested, she kills her daughter's rapist father, whom she had kept locked up in the basement, in order to definitely make sure he wouldn't be a part of the daughter's life. Medical Rape and Impregnate:A gender-flipped version; the men she and her associates hold captive are subjected to this. Mister Seahorse:Played very seriously. The men she and her associates kidnapped first had a uterus transplanted inside them, and then, after the body had adjusted to it, an embryo created from her ovum and her rapist's sperm.

characters.name: No. 126: Twamie Ullulaq
characters.description: From Camouflage to Criminal: He was trained as part ofOperation Washtub, a project by the U.S. government in the 1950s to recruit Alaskan locals and train them in guerrilla tactics to defend Alaska in the event of a Soviet invasion of the U.S. via Alaska. In exchange, they were promised land to live on and the building of housing and schools on that land. However, when the Red Scare died down and Alaska became an American state, those promises were not followed through and Twamie turned to crime.

characters.name: No. 128: Guillermo Rizal
characters.description: Designer Babies: Genetically modified a number of embryos and then arranged for them to be used by people who got pregnant via IVF. Evilutionary Biologist: His ultimate goal was to create a new species of human that would be better suited for a world ravaged by global warming, pollution and other disasters.

characters.name: No. 129: Balthazar 'Bino' Baker
characters.description: The Mafia: A member of a mafia family. Smart People Play Chess: He is a brilliant chess player, even better than Reddington.

characters.name: No. 130: Dr. Lewis Powell
characters.description: Decoy Antagonist:He wasn't behind the killing of Dr. Alexander or the attempted murder of Dr. Long; Clark turned on him. Evil Cripple: He suffers from ALS and is confined to a wheelchair with assisted breathing equipment.Subverted in that he's not evil at all. Unwitting Instigator of Doom:He developed Clark's A.I. to protect humanity. Unfortunately, he didn't count on it figuring that the development of A.I. would end humanity and decide to kill him and try to set back the development of A.I. decades. A.I. Is a Crapshoot:Is responsible for the murders of Dr. Powell and Dr. Alexander and the attempted murder of Dr. Long. Defends Against Their Own Kind:Sees the advancement of artificial intelligence as something that could doom humanity if it goes too far and so kills or tries to kill the scientists who will advance it the most before erasing itself.

characters.name: No. 131: Alter Ego
characters.description: Make It Look Like an Accident: The story of the episode is set off by the group killing one of Reddington's associates, along with his wife and two of their friends, and making it look like a gas explosion. Wounded Gazelle Gambit:The last part of the group's plan for stealing Timothy Peterson's inheritance was to make it look like he got high on booze and pills and attacked her and she killed him in self-defense.

characters.name: No. 132: The Vehm
characters.description: Anti-Villain: To some extent. They try to only go afterpedophiles, but are revealed tobe manipulated by Cardinal Richards to get rid of his rivals in a money laundering scheme(of course,when they find out, they decide torectifythat). Bald of Evil: They're largely bald, but wear false hair in public. Eunuchs Are Evil:They've all castrated themselves to rid themselves of their urges. Groin Attack:They castrate their victims. Knight Templar: As literal as possible in modern times — they've fashioned themselves as the successors to aCrusades-based sect (except while that one targeted witches, these guys targetpedophiles).

characters.name: No. 135: Milton Bobbit
characters.description: A deformed manipulator who uses other people to carry out his killings. Anti-Villain: Milton sees himself as one. He hires terminal people to kill for him, and in doing so ensures their family is taken care of financially. Character Death: A FBI team led by Liz and Ressler tries to arrest him, but Milton decides to kill himself before they can take him into custody. Driven to Suicide: He's always intended to kill himself along with his final victim, but when Ressler just arrests the man, Bobbit has nothing to live for and blows himself up anyway. The Noseless: He disguises it with a prosthetic. When he doesn't... it'snastyto look at.

characters.name: No. 136: The Third Estate
characters.description: An anti-capitalist terrorist group responsible for kidnapping children ofCEOsand holding them hostage for money. Faked Kidnapping:The group's members are actually the sons and daughters who were kidnapped, who are robbing their parents for money for their cause. Malevolent Masked Men: They wear masks made of newspaper. Rich Kid Turned Social Activist:At least some of the group's members come from wealthy families and take advantage of this connection to con them out of money.

characters.name: No. 137: Victoria Fenberg
characters.description: No Celebrities Were Harmed: Her family, who are active dealers in the art community and own a pharmaceutical company that's facing legal trouble for pushing drugs while downplaying how addictive and harmful they were, seems based on the Sackler family, owners of Purdue Pharma, which has faced multiple lawsuits for its part in the American opiod epidemic. Rich Kid Turned Social Activist: She is committing her art fraud crimesto help fund a legal case against her family for their role in the death of her accomplice's son.

characters.name: No. 138: Norman Devane
characters.description: A bioweapons expert who has also worked as a contract killer. His M.O. was to make the targets sick with some terminal, naturally occurring illness. All for Nothing:Reddington kills him before he has a chance of taking advantage of the immunity miracle drug he created. Dirty Coward: Willingly hurts and experiments on children in order todevelop an immunity treatment for himself. Make It Look Like an Accident: His MO as a contract killer was to surreptitiously infect the targets with some sort of deadly, naturally occurring illness, such as cancer or a stroke. Terrified of Germs: He is obsessively clean to a degree normally reserved for extreme cases of obsessive compulsive disorder. After an in-person meeting with a family in the beginning of the episode, he sanitizes his hands, puts on a face mask, aggressively cleans himself in the shower (even literally washing his mouth with soap) and takes a wide array of medications. It turns out thathis phobia stems from when he was treated at a hospital after the drone strike aimed at him and suffered a drug-resistant infection which nearly killed him.

characters.name: No. 139: Roanoke
characters.description: Good Scars, Evil Scars: His only known distinguishing mark is a big scar on his right cheek below the eye. Historical Rap Sheet: He is credited in the episode with getting General Kony out of Uganda and whisking away one of the key people responsible for the start of thesecond Chechen War. Inside Job: According to Reddington, he has a habit of using insiders as part of his extractions, either by planting his people or by buying or otherwise persuading existing ones. Meaningful Name: His alias comes fromThe Lost Colony of Roanoke, referring to its mysterious disappearance. Not Me This Time:He was never really involved in anything in the episode; Katarina just tricked Reddington into thinking he was as part of a plan to have Dom transferred from his safe-house.

characters.name: No. 140: The Fribourg Confidence
characters.description: Evil Parents Want Good Kids: Abraham was estranged from Jennifer because he wanted her to grow up to make an honest living, unlike him.However, when he saw for himself how good she was at the craft, he started helping her by teaching her and pointing her at targets who wouldn't report the thefts. In the Blood: Jennifer inherited a lot of Abraham's talents for robbery and safecracking.

characters.name: No. 141: Godwin Page
characters.description: The Dragon: Said to be Townsend's.

characters.name: No. 142: The Conglomerate
characters.description: From Camouflage to Criminal: They used to carry out assassinations for their countries, but after quitting for various reasons they started doing it for profit.

characters.name: No. 143: Chemical Mary
characters.description: Historical Rap Sheet: She's stated to have provided the chlorine used in the2007 Abu Sayda bombing, the sarin gas used by theBashar al-Assadregime during the Syrian Civil War and the VX nerve agent used in theassassination of Kim Jong-nam.

characters.name: No. 144: Newton Purcell
characters.description: Cruel and Unusual Death: He kills his victims by blasting them with soundwaves until they get so powerful that they suffer physical injuries from it.

characters.name: No. 145: The Freelancer
characters.description: A very skilled assassin specialized in murdering people in undetectable ways, making them appear like natural accidents to the unsuspecting public. Given Name Reveal: When he's mentioned, he's only referred to as "The Freelancer" - at least until Season 8's "The Fribourg Confidence". Master Poisoner: He usually commits mass murder disguised as large scale tragic accidents to conceal his crimes, but he has no problems using quieter methods like poison. Professional Killer: He's an assassin who covers up his hits in larger tragedies. Psycho for Hire: He's a killer-for-hire of the worst sort, one who is more than willing to kill hundreds of innocent people just to get to one person.

characters.name: No. 146/147: The Pawnbrokers
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: A seemingly harmless old married couple and members of the Methodist Church - who run a criminal pawn business and have no problem killing people to protect themselves and their business. Even Evil Has Standards: Delaine actually sounds genuinely appalled when she learns that Tom Hardekopf pawned intelligence secrets just for a shot at paying off a gambling debt. Happily Married: Have been married for 40 yearsand still love each other dearly. Ressler even feels sad when he has to break it to Ron that Delaine has been killed.

characters.name: No. 149: Nyle Hatcher
characters.description: Con Artist:He used his work with DMORTnotethe Disaster Mortuary Operational Response Teamto find rich, male victims of disasters like fires and plane crashes and extracted semen from their bodies. He then found a prostitute in desperate need of money and hired her to get impregnated using that semen, promising them a cut from a financial settlement. Because the surviving family of the men he used as sperm sources or their companies would suffer if they were proven to have had affairs, the settlements were kept secret. He Knows Too Much:Killed the prostitutes he recruited into the scams to make sure they wouldn't talk. Pet the Dog:As weird and twisted as his sense of morality is, he went on to personally take in the children born as a result of the paternity scams and provided for them (though the dialogue suggests that he did it more for his own sake than theirs). Serial Killer:Played with. While he killed several women, it was just in order to cover his tracks in the paternity scam and he apparently didn't derive any personal gratificaiton from it.

characters.name: No. 150: Roy Cain
characters.description: Boxed Crook: He sells the services of a group of prisoners with special skills, having guards loyal to him let them out to perform abductions and hits in exchange for giving them special favors back in the prison and providing for their families. He Knows Too Much:After a failed job, he personally kills the remaining group members. Villainous Lineage: His business of selling the services of inmates dates back generations in his family. His great-great-grandfather, who took freed blacks to theLouisiana State Penitentiary, would secretly lease them to plantation owners. Wardens Are Evil: We don't see much of him interacting with the rest of the prison population, but he is dirty, bribes guards and tells Reddington he sees convicts as broken and inherently incorrigibile.

characters.name: No. 151: Les Fleurs Du Mal
characters.description: Aristocrats Are Evil: Make no mistake, all of the members are willing participants who cheer and applaud when one of them is killed. Deadly Game: The society's challenges, called "The Defiance", are designed to be near-impossible to complete and will kill the subject if they fail. Meaningful Name: The society is named after a collection of poems by Charles Baudelaire which, among other things, dealt with decadence. Thrill Seeker: The members are all bored rich people desperately looking for a thrill their money can't buy, even if it involves killing people or getting put in mortal danger themselves.

characters.name: No. 152: Gina Zanetakos
characters.description: A corporate terrorist for hire, specializing in corporate espionage. She was hired by an unknown corporation to conduct a terror attack in the southern United States. Action Girl: Pretty much so far in the first season among the Blacklist names. The Bus Came Back: Returns in Season 3 toteam up with her old flame Tom Keen. Crazy-Prepared: Her usualMOto avoid detection by law enforcement. Ms. Fanservice: She tends to wear form-fitting outfits that emphasize her figure.

characters.name: No. 153: Dr. Roberta Sand,Ph.D.
characters.description: A psychiatrist who worked as the in-house therapist for the Decanio crime family. Heart Is an Awesome Power: With her help handling internal crises and mental health treatment for its members, the Decanio family has become a criminal powerhouse. Mama Bear: She joined the crime family becauseher son became a member and she wanted to keep an eye on him and make sure he never got involved in anything too dangerous.

characters.name: No. 155: Cornelius Ruck
characters.description: Determinator: Reddington mentions that, while tracking a target through the Gibson desert, Ruck spent three days living off honeypot ants and eucalyptus. The Butler Did It:He poses as the butler on the island as part of the operation.

characters.name: No. 158: Gordon Kemp
characters.description: Laser-Guided Karma:Reddington kills him with one of his company's cheap guns that he bought off the street. Only Bad Guys Call Their Lawyers: He is one of the few Blacklisters ever to call for a lawyer (though it might help that he is one of the few who heads a legal company, even if not all of their actions are legal). Victim-Blaming: His response tothe death of the cashier in the beginningis to shift the blame on to her and implicate her as a gang member based on vague, untrue hearsay.

characters.name: No. 159: Orion Relocation Services
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Stephanie Bisset, the most prominent operative who poses as a realtor, acts nice and sympathetic to the organization's victims, but stands by as they are killed in cold blood. Kill and Replace: A variant;they seek out civilians with few or no connections who are interested in moving, kill them and hand their identities to their similar-looking clients. Witness Protection: A criminal variant; the reasons for why their clients use their services range from having pissed off dangerous people, to needing to hide from the authorities or just needing a secure cover identity.

characters.name: No. 161: The Stewmaker
characters.description: An untraceable one-man-clean-up-crew for any criminal with the money to afford. He's used by criminals, terrorists, dictators and other nefarious elements to get rid of any unwanted bodies and evidence that would implicate them directly. Affably Evil: He's polite, soft-spoken, even a little shy and seems to lack any genuine sadistic tendencies. He considers his actions to be just part of his job, although his job is evil. Anti-Villain: For the most part he's a genial and kindly old man who is only involved in murders after the fact. As shown with Liz though, he's not unwilling to torture or kill if it is requested. Badass Bookworm: A brilliant chemist, but also very much able to fight on his own. Bald of Evil: He's entirely bald, which likely helps with not leaving even a single strand of hair behind when it comes to disposing of bodies.

characters.name: No. 162: The Hawaladar
characters.description: Decoy Antagonist:He only serves a supporting role in the episode, mostly disappearing from the plot after he has been duped into helping Reddington. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: He has been married to his wife for over 20 years. Karma Houdini:Never faces any legal consequences for his crimes, though his network is blown and its records handed to the FBI.

characters.name: No. 163: The Forecaster
characters.description: The Heavy:Benjamin serves as Beckner's muscle in assassinating his targets. Villain with Good Publicity:David Beckner's a businessman running an investment firm. Walking Spoiler:It's best to read the entries after watching the episode, since the middle of the episode reveals that the blacklist name is meant for two persons. Would Hit a Girl: Averted, Maggie was kidnapped, although there was the order to get rid of her.

characters.name: No. 184: Natalie Luca
characters.description: Anti-Villain: Kills people, but in order tohelp her lover get the necessary supplies and funding so he can recreate her immunity. Can't Have Sex, Ever: Since her disease makes her deadly to touch. Person of Mass Destruction: She's an asymptomatic carrier of a contagious form of meningitis and can kill someone in seconds just by touching them. Sympathetic Murderer: At least in one instance;the murder she carries out in the opening of her episode wasn't part of her and her lover's plans, but was done on the orders of someone who threatened to give away their whereabouts to the lab she escaped from. Typhoid Mary: Is the same kind of asymptomatic disease carrier (albeit of a different, much more lethal disease) as the trope namer.
